title: A Giant Eye in Space
paragraphs: The James Webb Space Telescope is one of the biggest telescopes ever sent into space. It was launched on Christmas Day in two thousand twenty one. Today it floats about one and a half million kilometres from Earth. Its job is to look far away and far back in time. Light from far away takes a very long time to arrive.

The telescope looks at infrared light, which people cannot see with their eyes. Its main mirror is covered with gold and made of eighteen smaller pieces. Together, they work like one huge mirror, about six and a half metres wide.

Webb stays near a point in space where the pull of the Sun and Earth helps keep it steady. Scientists use the telescope to study faraway stars and very old galaxies. It sends its pictures back to Earth so people everywhere can enjoy them.
